mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP signals strengthening economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in industrial production signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts signals increased consumer demand, which boosts economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and CPI increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to expected monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.3%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of increasing PAYEMS and decreasing UNRATE on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP increases by more than 2% annually and housing starts increase by more than 10% in a month, it signals a strong demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 2% annually and HOUST increases > 10% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of increasing GDPC1 and HOUST on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
